body_markdown:
A Dutch health and drug monitoring organisation has issued an urgent warning after ecstasy pills designed in the shape of US President Donald Trump's head were found to contain a potentially deadly chemical.


The Trimbos Institute, a Dutch organisation focused on mental health and drug use, issued a "red alert" in August 2026 after several unusual pills were submitted to drug testing centres in the Netherlands. Laboratory analysis reportedly found that the tablets contained a very high concentration of PMMA, a substance that can produce dangerous and potentially fatal effects.


The institute has strongly advised people not to consume the pills.


## Trump-Shaped Ecstasy Pills Trigger Dutch Health Warning


The tablets have been manufactured in a distinctive shape resembling Donald Trump's face. According to images released by the Trimbos Institute, one version has a green front featuring Trump's facial features, while the reverse side is red and includes the markings "Trump" and "NL".


Another version photographed by the institute has yellow and blue colouring.


Despite their unusual appearance, health officials say the major concern is not the design but the chemical composition of the tablets.


The pills were reportedly brought to drug testing facilities in the Netherlands during August. Testing indicated that they contained a very high level of PMMA, also known as para-methoxymethamphetamine.


The Trimbos Institute warned that the tablets should not be taken under any circumstances because of the risk of severe poisoning.


## What Is PMMA?


PMMA is a synthetic stimulant that is chemically related to MDMA, the primary psychoactive substance commonly associated with ecstasy.


However, PMMA behaves differently from MDMA. One significant concern is that its effects can take longer to appear. Someone who does not immediately feel the expected effects may mistakenly believe that the dose is too weak and take more of the substance.


That delay can increase the risk of a dangerous overdose.


The Trimbos Institute has warned that PMMA can cause serious physical effects, including a dangerously elevated body temperature. Severe overheating can lead to life-threatening complications.


Other possible symptoms associated with PMMA poisoning can include nausea, a rapid heartbeat and seizures.


The delayed onset of effects is particularly concerning because people may consume additional tablets before the initial dose has fully taken effect.


## Warning Issued After Pills Were Submitted for Testing


The Dutch institute said several examples of the Trump-shaped tablets had been handed in at drug checking centres during August.


Drug testing services allow people to submit substances for analysis and can help public health organisations identify unexpectedly dangerous drugs circulating in the recreational drug market.


Following laboratory testing, the Trimbos Institute released photographs of the tablets and issued its red alert.


The organisation said there were no reported cases of deaths or serious illnesses linked to the pills at the time of its warning.


However, the absence of reported cases does not mean the tablets are safe. The institute's warning was based on the chemical contents identified during testing and the potentially severe effects associated with PMMA.


## Why PMMA in Ecstasy Pills Can Be Dangerous


Ecstasy tablets can contain different substances and concentrations, even when pills look similar or carry the same logo or design.


This creates a particular risk for people who assume that the appearance of a pill tells them what is inside it.


PMMA can produce stimulant effects, but its effects may appear later than those associated with MDMA. This creates a dangerous situation in which a person may take more of the drug while waiting for the initial dose to take effect.


A higher amount can then enter the body as the substances begin to take effect.


Potential symptoms of serious stimulant poisoning include a rapid heartbeat, nausea, seizures and severe overheating. In serious cases, overheating can become life-threatening.


The Dutch warning therefore focuses on avoiding the specific tablets rather than relying on their colour, shape or branding as an indication of their contents.


## Ecstasy Remains Popular in the Netherlands


The warning comes in a country where ecstasy remains a well-known recreational drug despite its illegal status.


A Dutch government report published in 2024 said ecstasy continued to be popular as a party drug. According to figures cited in that report, approximately 550,000 people had used ecstasy at least once in 2022, described as a record figure at the time.


The popularity of ecstasy has also contributed to the importance of drug monitoring and testing services in the Netherlands.


Dutch drug testing programmes can identify substances that contain unexpected or particularly hazardous chemicals. Public health alerts can then be issued when a significant risk is detected.


## Trump-Inspired Ecstasy Pills Have Appeared Before


The use of Donald Trump's image on ecstasy tablets is not entirely new.


In 2017, German authorities seized thousands of ecstasy tablets shaped like Trump's head. Reports at the time said police confiscated approximately 5,000 orange or carrot-coloured pills.


The tablets were reportedly promoted online with a slogan referencing Trump's political campaign branding.


The latest Dutch warning involves different pills, and the Trimbos Institute's concern is specifically connected to the presence of PMMA.


The recurrence of political figures and celebrities as designs on recreational drugs highlights how pill manufacturers can use recognisable images to market or distinguish their products. However, the appearance of a tablet provides no reliable indication of its chemical contents or safety.


## What Health Officials Are Warning About


The central message from the Trimbos Institute is straightforward: people should not consume the Trump-shaped pills identified in its warning.


The presence of a high concentration of PMMA makes the tablets potentially dangerous. The delayed effects associated with the substance can also make accidental overdose more likely.


Anyone who develops severe symptoms after taking an unknown or potentially contaminated substance should seek urgent medical attention.


Symptoms such as seizures, severe overheating, a very rapid heartbeat or serious deterioration in consciousness can require emergency treatment.


People should also avoid assuming that a pill is safe because it looks familiar or has a recognisable logo, colour or shape. Illicit tablets can contain substances that differ substantially from what users expect.


## Key Takeaway


The Dutch Trimbos Institute has issued a red alert over Trump-shaped ecstasy pills after testing found a very high amount of PMMA in several tablets submitted to drug testing centres.


The organisation says the pills can pose a serious health risk and has advised people not to use them.


PMMA is related to MDMA but can have a delayed effect, potentially encouraging people to take more before the first dose has fully taken effect. The resulting overdose can cause severe symptoms, including overheating and seizures.


At the time of the warning, Dutch officials said there were no reported deaths or serious illnesses associated with the tablets. Nevertheless, the chemical findings prompted the urgent public health alert.


The incident is another reminder that the appearance of an illicit pill cannot reliably indicate what it contains. Public health organisations continue to monitor recreational drug supplies to identify dangerous substances and warn the public when significant risks are discovered.
